html.en:
Hardware = all the physical components of a computer — the parts you can touch.
Software = all the programs that tell the physical components what to do.

rows.en: The brain of the computer. Does all the calculations.
Holds the data the computer is using right now.
Keeps your files when the computer is switched off.
Draws the images on the screen. Important for games.

html.en:
💿 Software components

  • System software — the operating system (Windows, macOS, Android).
  • Application software — word processing, spreadsheet, presentation and video editing software.
Hardware and software are complementary. A computing device can only produce useful outputs when both work together.
⭐ The 5 factors when choosing hardware and software

rows.en: What the user wants to use it for — what a device can do. It must meet your requirements.
Whether the hardware and software can work together.
Can you afford it? The most expensive is not always the best.
How fast the processor works, measured in gigahertz (GHz).
What something looks like — colour, shape, design.

html.en:
Digital content is anything that can be stored or sent digitally — text, audio, video files, graphics, animations and images.

A server is a computer that provides services on a network. ← learn this sentence word for word.

🗄️ What servers store

  • Photographs and images — so people can share pictures and photo albums.
  • Messages — mainly text, but they can include images and emojis.
  • Websites — the files and data for websites.
  • Email messages — Gmail, Hotmail and Yahoo! Mail store them on servers.
  • Online software — like Google Docs™, used remotely and saved on Google’s servers.
  • Online games — each game generally has its own server.
  • Video content — movies, TV shows, music videos.
  • Audio content — music, podcasts and audio books. Music is the most popular form of audio.

▶️ Streaming
Streaming is when a digital file is sent a few seconds at a time from the server. You can start watching or listening while the rest of the file is still being sent.

rows.en: Sent a few seconds at a time
The whole file is copied first
You must wait for it to finish
Can be live, while an event is happening

html.en: The trap: “Streamed content is automatically stored on the user’s device.” → FALSE. It is automatically deleted.

Any network that is not connected using wires sends and receives data using radio waves.

📻 Radio waves

  • Radio waves are just like light waves — but we cannot see them.
  • They are all around us all the time.
  • They travel through the air, in all directions, and are picked up by a receiver.
  • They travel at the speed of light — that is why huge amounts of information move so quickly.
  • Radio waves used for Wi-Fi can travel long distances.

🔁 How the data actually gets to you — the chain
Internet → (wires) → router → converts data into radio waves → antenna → air → adapter inside your device → software turns it back into music / video / text

rows.en: Receives data from the internet through wires and converts that data into radio waves, which it transmits via its antenna.
Built into or attached to a digital device. It acts as both a transmitter and a receiver, and converts radio waves back into the original data.

html.en:
Exam trap: “Which device converts the data coming from the internet into a radio wave?” → the ROUTER, not the adapter.
“What sends Wi-Fi signals?” → the adapter (acting as the transmitter). “What receives Wi-Fi signals?” → the adapter (acting as the receiver).

📱 Cellular networks

  • They use exactly the same principle, just a different type of radio wave.
  • The waves carry data between a smartphone and a nearby base station.
  • Each base station is connected to the internet by wires.
  • They let a large number of portable devices communicate over large distances.

🚿 Bandwidth

Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be sent and received in a fixed amount of time.
It is given in kilobits per second (Kbps), megabits per second (Mbps) or gigabits per second (Gbps).

The water pipe: bandwidth is like the diameter of a pipe bringing water to your home. A wider pipe lets more water flow per second — more bandwidth lets more data flow per second. Bandwidth is one of several factors that affect the performance of a network.

Bandwidth has to be shared among all the devices on the network. More devices = less bandwidth each = reduced performance.

1 device → 54 Mbps  ·  2 devices → 27 Mbps each  ·  3 devices → 18 Mbps each
“Internet rush hour” is usually at night, when everyone is back home from work or school and all the devices are online at once.

html.en: The classic trap: a Club Code like BO101 looks like it has numbers in it — but it is a combination of letters and numbers and it will never be used in a calculation, so its data type is Text.

That finished table has 4 fields (columns) and 5 records (rows). The Club Code uniquely identifies each club — needed because two records can share the same data item (two people with the same name), and then the database cannot retrieve the right record.

✔️ Data Validation — how you set the data type

  1. Type the field names into the spreadsheet (row 1).
  2. Select the range of cells for that field (e.g. A2:A6).
  3. Open Data ▸ Data Validation.
  4. Under Allow, choose the type — e.g. Text length, Data: equal to, Length: 6 for a 6-character club code.
  5. Click OK, then repeat for every other field.
In Spanish Excel: Longitud del texto · igual a · 6. Same dialog, same idea.

🔍 The Find feature (phrase searching, page 98)

  1. Click Find & Select in the Home ribbon, or press Ctrl + F (Ctrl + B in Spanish Excel).
  2. The Find and Replace dialog box opens.
  3. Type the keyword — e.g. Cake — in the Find what box.
  4. Click Find All.
search: to look for. The Find feature searches a spreadsheet using keywords or phrases — much faster than reading through a large database by hand.

html.en: Supermarket table: Product Name → Text · Product Cost ($7.50) → Number (or Currency) · Quantity Sold (3) → Number · Date Sold (29/7/2023) → Date
Industries use data every day to solve problems, make informed decisions and monitor processes. The three industries in your book are health, sales and manufacturing.

🏥 Health

  • Patient record keeping — contact details, treatment and diagnosis stored in a database, so doctors can follow each patient's history. Essential in emergencies.
  • Health tracking — wearable technology records vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure) and activity (steps, distance walked). Helps save the lives of ‘at risk’ patients.
  • Medical research — data helps scientists find cures and test whether new medicines are working.

🛒 Sales

  • Stock control and advertisements — data shows how many of each product sold, so shops can reorder stock and advertise the most popular products.
  • Customer service — feedback on product quality and delivery time shows retailers what to improve.

🏭 Manufacturing

  • Control of machinery — most factories are automated. Robotic arms use data (colour, size) to make every product the same way.
  • Data on noise, heat and vibration shows when a machine needs maintenance — so it does not break down.
  • Customer satisfaction — data shows what customers want, e.g. which car colour is most popular.

html.en:
🗓️ A 5-day plan to be ready

Short sessions beat one long panic session. 25–35 minutes a day is plenty.

⭐ The marks students throw away every year

  1. Calling the monitor or the keyboard "software". If you can touch it, it is hardware.
  2. Mixing up functionality (what it can do) and aesthetics (what it looks like).
  3. Writing the storage units in the wrong order. It is bit → byte → KB → MB → GB → TB.
  4. Forgetting that 1 byte = 1 character — and that spaces and punctuation are characters too.
  5. Saying streamed content is saved on your device. It is deleted automatically once you play it.
  6. Saying the adapter converts internet data into radio waves. That is the router. The adapter is inside the device.
  7. Saying radio waves travel through cables. Radio waves travel through the air; the cables carry data to the router.
  8. Saying bandwidth is "speed". Bandwidth is how much data can be sent in a fixed amount of time.
  9. Mixing up fields (columns) and records (rows).
  10. Giving a Club Code like BO101 the Number data type. Letters + numbers = Text.
  11. In Scratch, forgetting that turn = 360 ÷ number of sides (triangle 120°, square 90°).
  12. Leaving a question blank. Always write something.
The night before: don't learn anything new. Re-read the purple rule boxes in Learn, do 10 quick questions in Practice, then stop. Sleep is worth more marks than another hour of studying. 😴

In the exam: read every question twice. Underline the question word (state, explain, name, why). If it says explain, write a because… sentence. If it says state two, write two — not one, not three. ✍️
